image_description: A grey whale breaching or surfacing in blue ocean water. The head and rostrum are visible emerging from the water, showing mottled grey skin with white barnacle patches. A pectoral flipper is also visible breaking the surface. There is a prominent watermark text '© Roi Hlaker' across the center of the image.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is partially submerged and viewed from a side/low angle; the top of the rostrum where blowholes would be located is not clearly visible or distinguishable due to water splash and angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin on the head and flipper clearly shows the characteristic mottled grey pattern with distinct white callosities/barnacle patches.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The posterior back and dorsal region are completely submerged or outside the frame; only the anterior head and one flipper are visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the head checkpoint, the visible skin texture matches the description of mottled grey with white barnacle patches.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed or submerged; baleen plates are internal structures not visible in this external view.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: One pectoral flipper is clearly visible breaking the surface; it appears broad and paddle-shaped consistent with grey whale anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail flukes are completely submerged and not visible in the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin on the head and flipper exhibits the rough texture and raised white callosities typical of grey whales.
